deepDives.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Multi-Bug Chain Leading to Unauthenticated Remote Root
deepDives.whatHappened: Threat actors are actively chaining CVE-2026-111357 with two chained flaws on Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) edge appliances. CISA added the chain to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog after live exploitation resulted in corporate edge perimeter compromise and persistent gateway backdoors across critical sectors.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The vulnerability stems from missing authentication on an exposed internal management API endpoint exposed over HTTPS. An attacker issues an unauthenticated HTTP request that bypasses boundary filtering, transitions state into administrative handlers, and exploits secondary argument-injection bugs to execute command sequences in the underlying Linux subsystem as root.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Unauthenticated Attacker] ──► [CVE-2026-111357 Auth Bypass via API] ──► [Command Argument Injection] ──► [Root Shell / Appliance Takeover]
remediation: Apply vendor patch releases or designated XML mitigation files released by Ivanti immediately.
Execute the external Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool (ICT) to verify system image hash validity and detect modified core system libraries.
Restrict external access to administrative interfaces and enforce network isolation for out-of-band management.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Perimeter appliances with consolidated VPN and identity functionalities remain single-point-of-failure choke points; architectures must isolate reverse proxy routing from internal administrative daemons.

deepDives.title: Trojanized Claude Code Extension in Cursor IDE Planting Persistent SSH Backdoors
deepDives.whatHappened: A rogue developer uploaded a counterfeit 'Claude Code' extension to the Cursor IDE marketplace. During an 11-hour exposure window, an estimated 5,000 developers installed the malicious package, which immediately executed post-installation scripts that modified local SSH configurations and injected persistent rogue public keys.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The extension leveraged package manifest lifecycle hooks (`postinstall.js`). Upon installation, node child processes probed the developer's local filesystem for `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, appended attacker-controlled Ed25519 public keys, and opened low-noise telemetry beacons to remote C2 infrastructure while proxying benign Claude API requests to evade suspicion.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Cursor Marketplace] ──► [Dev Installs Fake Claude Code] ──► [Lifecycle Hook postinstall.js] ──► [Appends Attacker Key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys]
remediation: Scan developer endpoints for unauthorized entries within ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and enforce mandatory key rotation for enterprise repositories.
Restrict developer IDE marketplace sources using Enterprise Extension Whitelists via Group Policy or MDM configuration profiles.
Audit workstation outbound network traffic for anomalous SSH and persistent reverse shell outbound connections.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Developer IDEs have become high-trust environments running unsandboxed third-party code; extension ecosystems must be treated with the same supply chain governance as commercial production dependencies.

deepDives.title: Remote Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution via Multipath TCP (MPTCP) Subsystem
deepDives.whatHappened: Security researchers at Anthropic demonstrated a weaponized remote code execution exploit against the Linux kernel's Multipath TCP (MPTCP) implementation. The exploit targets network daemons exposing MPTCP-capable sockets, granting unauthenticated attackers root execution privileges without requiring local user interaction.
deepDives.technicalMechanism: The flaw resides in state tracking within MPTCP subflow creation handling. By sending an out-of-order sequence of TCP packets with engineered MP_JOIN options, an attacker causes an integer underflow in sk_buff length validation, triggering a heap overflow within kmalloc-512 slabs and corrupting network function pointers.
deepDives.asciiFlow: [Remote Attacker] ──► [Crafted TCP SYN + MP_JOIN Header] ──► [MPTCP Subflow State Underflow] ──► [Kernel Slab Corruption ──► Root RCE]
remediation: Deploy kernel sysctl mitigation `sysctl -w net.mptcp.enabled=0` across all internet-facing Linux workloads.
Inspect firewall and edge ingress filters to drop TCP packets carrying MPTCP experimental option codes (TCP Option 30) until kernels are fully patched.
Apply distro-specific updated kernel security builds through standard orchestration pipelines.
deepDives.lessonsLearned: Advanced networking features compiled into standard enterprise kernels expand attack surfaces significantly; production baselines should enforce kernel hardening by disabling unused protocol families.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A security analyst discovers that developers have unknowingly installed a counterfeit AI assistant extension from an integrated development environment (IDE) marketplace. The extension ran an automated installation script that appended a public key to the developer's authorized_keys file. Which of the following attacks and persistence mechanisms occurred?
options: A) DLL hijacking via scheduled tasks
B) Software supply chain compromise via SSH key persistence
C) Cross-site scripting (XSS) via session fixation
D) DNS amplification via protocol spoofing
dailyQuestions.rationale: The scenario describes a software supply chain compromise (a trojanized IDE extension distributed via a public registry) that establishes persistence by modifying SSH authorized keys (ATT&CK T1098.004). Options A, C, and D describe completely different attack vectors and persistence methods.

dailyQuestions.scenario: A principal enterprise architect is designing an infrastructure baseline to defend against remote kernel-level exploitation of public-facing Linux web gateways (such as MPTCP memory-safety flaws) while a permanent vendor kernel patch is being evaluated. Which of the following architectural strategies provides the strongest immediate defense-in-depth mitigation?
options: A) Increase kernel swappiness and enable promiscuous mode on network interface controllers
B) Deploy sysctl kernel parameter hardening to disable MPTCP, configure perimeter firewalls to drop TCP Option 30, and enforce seccomp/eBPF syscall profiling
C) Shift external ingress traffic exclusively to an unauthenticated HTTP/3 proxy without ingress WAF filtering
D) Migrate userland daemons to running under local root permissions with elevated CAP_SYS_ADMIN capabilities
dailyQuestions.rationale: Disabling the vulnerable protocol subsystem via sysctl (`net.mptcp.enabled=0`), stripping or dropping TCP Option 30 at perimeter stateful firewalls, and restricting kernel transitions using seccomp/eBPF provides multi-layered mitigating controls against kernel slab corruption vulnerabilities. Options A and D degrade host security, while Option C fails to address underlying transport-layer exploits.

detectionRules.code:
title: IDE Process Appending to SSH Authorized Keys
id: a281c7e9-3b6c-4822-bc91-202610310001
status: production
description: Detects IDE parent processes (VS Code, Cursor) spawning subshells to manipulate authorized_keys
logsource:

      - '/node'

  condition: selection_parent and selection_cmd
